speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are an infant presenting with recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing; could you tell me exactly when these breathing difficulties occur, such as during feeding, crying, or sleeping?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The worsening of symptoms specifically during neck flexion is highly suggestive of a vascular ring or compression. Given the age and history of vomiting with feeding, do you notice any difficulty with swallowing liquids or solids, or does the child choke frequently?

REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_Flexion_Xray

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vascular Ring (likely Double Aortic Arch) causing tracheal compression and esophageal obstruction.
